subject: physics
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Which of the following is a magnetic material?
questions.explain: Iron is a magnetic material, as are steel, cobalt and nickel.

questions.q: Where is the magnetic field of a bar magnet strongest?
options: At the centre of the magnet
questions.explain: The field is strongest at the poles, where the field lines are closest together.

questions.q: Outside a bar magnet, magnetic field lines are drawn pointing...
options: from the north pole to the south pole
from the south pole to the north pole
from both poles towards the centre
from the centre outwards to both poles
questions.explain: By convention, field lines run from north to south outside the magnet.

questions.q: What happens when the north pole of one magnet is brought close to the north pole of another?
questions.explain: Like poles repel, while unlike poles attract.

questions.q: A long coil of wire that produces a magnetic field when a current flows through it is called a...
questions.explain: A solenoid is a coil of wire that behaves like a bar magnet when carrying a current.

questions.q: Which change would increase the strength of an electromagnet?
options: Decreasing the number of turns on the coil
Increasing the current in the coil
Reducing the current in the coil
questions.explain: A larger current, more turns or adding an iron core all strengthen an electromagnet.

questions.q: The size of the force on a current-carrying conductor in a magnetic field is given by which equation?
questions.explain: Force equals magnetic flux density multiplied by current and by length of conductor.

questions.q: What is the unit of magnetic flux density?
questions.explain: Magnetic flux density B is measured in tesla (T).

questions.q: When using Fleming's left-hand rule for the motor effect, the first finger points in the direction of the...
questions.explain: First finger = Field, seCond finger = Current, thuMb = Motion (force).

questions.q: The force on a current-carrying wire in a magnetic field is greatest when the wire is...
questions.explain: The force is maximum when the wire is at right angles to the field and zero when parallel to it.

questions.q: In a simple DC motor, what is the purpose of the split-ring commutator?
options: To increase the voltage supplied to the coil
To reverse the current in the coil every half turn
To reduce the current to a safe level
To convert AC into DC before the coil
questions.explain: Reversing the current each half turn keeps the coil rotating in the same direction.

questions.q: A wire of length 0.10 m carries a current of 2.0 A at right angles to a magnetic field of flux density 0.50 T. What is the force on the wire?
A conductor of length 0.30 m lies at right angles to a magnetic field of flux density 0.20 T. If the force on it is 0.60 N, what current flows?
How can the direction of the force on a current-carrying wire in a magnetic field be reversed?
options: By reversing the direction of the current
By increasing the strength of the field
questions.explain: Reversing either the current or the field direction reverses the force.

questions.q: Transformers only work with...
questions.explain: Transformers need a continually changing magnetic field, so they only work with AC.

questions.q: A voltage is induced in a coil when...
options: a steady current flows through it
the magnetic field through it is changing
it is connected to a battery
it is held still in a constant field
questions.explain: Electromagnetic induction requires a changing magnetic field through the coil.

questions.q: In a step-up transformer, the potential difference across the secondary coil is...
options: greater than that across the primary
less than that across the primary
equal to that across the primary
questions.explain: A step-up transformer has more turns on the secondary, giving a higher output voltage.

questions.q: Which change would increase the size of the voltage induced when a magnet is moved into a coil?
options: Using fewer turns on the coil
questions.explain: A faster movement, a stronger magnet or more turns all increase the induced voltage.

questions.q: A transformer has 100 turns on the primary coil and 500 turns on the secondary coil. If the primary voltage is 12 V, what is the secondary voltage?
questions.explain: Vp/Vs = Np/Ns, so Vs = 12 × 500/100 = 60 V.

questions.q: A transformer is 100% efficient. The primary has a voltage of 230 V and a current of 1.0 A. If the secondary voltage is 23 V, what is the secondary current?
questions.explain: For an ideal transformer VpIp = VsIs, so Is = (230 × 1.0)/23 = 10 A.

specSource: CCEA GCSE Physics (2017) specification; Magnetism & Electromagnetism
